outcomes: An application composes one plugin and starts collecting page views and declared actions into its own Postgres
A visitor cannot be linked across UTC days without a consent-gated identifier, and no network address or raw user agent is ever stored
A page view or action that is retried by the browser, or re-sent with engagement, changes no aggregate
A sender learns nothing from the ingest answer, and a bot leaves no trace
A slow or unreachable database costs bounded memory and lost events, never a slow page
nonGoals: Visualisation, dashboards, or any read API (Putnami Cloud, later)
Cross-site tracking, fingerprinting beyond the daily hash, or any third-party egress
A Go runtime — there is no Go web layer; only the wire contract is shared
Web vitals, scroll depth, click autocapture (v2)
Governing consent UI — the application owns the banner and passes a consent callback

requirements.text: A page served from build output carries the tracker and this request's page-view id, injected into the response the handler produced, so a fully pre-rendered site collects sessions, engagement, and declared actions without double-counting the view the server already recorded; a page the React renderer produced is left untouched.
An event replayed by the browser, or re-sent to carry engagement, enriches the row it already wrote and leaves every counter, daily unique, and session aggregate unchanged.

No response path waits for the analytics sink: a page, a beacon, and a server-side track() return while the write is still pending, rows are held in a bounded queue that drops the oldest and counts them when it is full, and stop() drains what is left inside its deadline even when the database never answers.

An accepted ingest answers 202 whether every event was stored or every event was dropped, so the only statuses a sender can distinguish are transport faults: 400 for a body that is not JSON and 413 for a body over the size ceiling.
A request whose user agent matches the closed bot list receives no tracker bootstrap, mints no cookie, and writes no row.
A persistent visitor cookie exists only after the application's consent callback returned true, is signed server-side, and a cookie whose signature does not verify is treated as no cookie at all.

A client address and a raw user agent are consumed only to derive a daily-rotating hash and a coarse device family, and every column written to the database is a name the shared protocol vocabulary declares.
A request carrying Sec-GPC: 1, or DNT: 1 when the application respects it, is collected in cookieless mode however the plugin is configured.
An HTML page response records a server page view identified by a daily-rotating hash, sets no cookie, and hands the browser only the event id and route it needs to complete that view.

Raw events are deleted past their retention window by a bounded sweep that runs at most every ten minutes, and the scheduled mode contributes the database job that keeps expiry running when the application is idle.
The published browser graph reaches no server-only runtime import and no server implementation symbol, and the tracker it ships stays under 4 KiB gzipped.

The four tables live in the schema their datasource already has: analytics.schema when set, otherwise the schema another SQL migration source or sql() declares for that datasource, otherwise public. A workload that declares no schema keeps its migration bundle byte for byte, and a schema that contradicts the datasource's fails the build instead of the migration.
An action name the application did not declare, or a property outside the declared bounds, never reaches the database: the wire event is dropped and counted, and a server-side call raises.
